_comment: D-42 ratchet baseline. Every (company:scenario) pair whose terminal return exceeds
its cost of capital owes a structured excess_return_defence in the archetype impact
matrix. The pairs below assert one and do not yet declare it, each for a stated
reason. The list may only SHRINK: a pair that acquires a defence must be removed, and
a new undeclared pair fails the test. Same ratchet shape as tests/moat_role_baseline.json
Recorded 16 September 2026, when the D-42 diagnostic was first run. One of the fifteen
valuations asserting an excess return carried a defence at that moment, and it was prose.

dnl: Neither scenario carries a terminal_roic driver in the impact matrix at all, so the
excess return is emergent from the cash-flow assumptions and was never assessed.
Muddle Through is the headline valuation and asserts 226bp of excess over WACC, so
this is the most pressing of the three groups. Orderly Convergence was the only
valuation in the project with a defence and is now declared structurally; these two
need the same treatment, and the Orderly Convergence block is the worked example.
wbc: The bank matrix carries no terminal_roic driver for any scenario. In the section 15
fork the terminal return is a DECLARED input on the scenario overlay (terminal_roe)
rather than a matrix cell, so a defence has nowhere to live without deciding where a
bank's terminal-return defence belongs. That is a structural question, not an
omission to be filled in, and it needs Stephen rather than a session.
All six scenarios exceed Ke, by 95 to 295bp.
csl: Do not write a defence for a defect. CSL's 61-73% terminal return on new capital is
an artefact of D-53 being unimplemented: terminal_capex_pct_revenue is declared equal
to da_pct_revenue, so net terminal capex is zero and almost nothing is reinvested.
See M15. Implementing D-53 should drop the implied return into the range DNL occupies
and most of these pairs should leave this list by arithmetic rather than by being
justified. CSL also has no impact-matrix file, so there is no home for a defence yet.
